questions.q: What makes this course's capstone different from the individual courses that came before it?
options: It combines every tool from prior courses — SQL Server, SSIS, the warehouse, SSRS, and Power BI — into one end-to-end pipeline instead of teaching one tool in isolation
It only covers SQL Server and ignores every other tool
It replaces all prior course material with entirely new tools
It is purely theoretical, with no hands-on build
questions.explain: Every prior course taught one piece of the stack. This capstone is where those pieces become one working pipeline, built the way a real BI developer job would actually require.

questions.q: Why does this capstone model manufacturing work orders instead of Sales or Procurement?
options: Sales was already used by SSIS Development's and SSRS Development's capstones, and Procurement was already used by Data Modeling & Data Warehousing's capstone — work orders are a genuinely unused business process
AdventureWorks2012 has no sales data at all
Manufacturing is the only business process AdventureWorks tracks
Work orders are simpler than any other business process in AdventureWorks
questions.explain: Choosing a third, still-unused business process keeps this capstone a genuine modeling exercise rather than a repeat of a decision already made elsewhere in the catalog.

questions.q: What does a row in Production.WorkOrder actually represent?
options: A manufacturing instruction to produce a quantity of a product, including planned quantity, actual quantity, scrapped quantity, and a due date
A single retail sale to a customer
A purchase order sent to a vendor
An employee's timesheet entry
questions.explain: A work order tracks production, not sales or purchasing — it has a planned quantity, an actual quantity produced, a scrapped quantity, and a due date that may or may not be met.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what happens across Chapters 4 and 5 of this course, after the technical pipeline is built?
options: The finished capstone becomes the basis for a resume, a portfolio presentation, interview preparation, and a job search
The entire pipeline gets rebuilt from scratch using different tools
The course repeats T-SQL Development's content in full
Nothing — the course ends once the pipeline is validated
questions.explain: This is the final course in the Microsoft Data & BI Developer program — Chapters 4 and 5 turn the finished technical project into the material a real job search runs on: resume, portfolio, interviews, negotiation, and reading job postings.

questions.q: Which table would this capstone use to understand why a manufactured unit failed?
options: Production.ScrapReason
Sales.SalesOrderHeader
Purchasing.Vendor
HumanResources.Employee
questions.explain: Production.ScrapReason is the small reference table that records why a scrapped unit failed — exactly the kind of table a real dimension gets built from.
